content: The following are professional interpretations of the provided references: 1. Chang et al. (2007) conducted a study to estimate the protective concentration of anti-pneumococcal capsular polysaccharide antibodies, published in Vaccine. 2. Siber (1997) described methodologies for estimating serological correlates of protection in Developmental Biology Standards. 3. Ipsen (1946) analyzed circulating antitoxin levels at the onset of diphtheria in 425 patients, as reported in The Journal of Immunology. 4. Skendzel (1996) defined the protective antibody levels required for rubella immunity in American Journal of Clinical Pathology. 5. Dunning (2008) provided commentary on evaluating surrogate endpoints in vaccine development, as discussed in Statistics in Medicine. 6. 7. Dunning (2006) proposed a model for immunological correlates of protection in Statistics in Medicine. 8. Forrest et al. (2008) investigated the correlation between cellular immune responses and protection against culture-confirmed influenza in young children, published in Clinical Vaccine Immunology. 9. Slifka (2004) reviewed immunological memory to viral infections in Current Opinion in Immunology. 10. Fernandez et al. (2000) studied the prevention of Haemophilus influenzae type b colonization through vaccination and its correlation with serum anti-capsular IgG concentrations, as reported in The Journal of Infectious Diseases. 11. Edwards and Decker (2008) discussed pertussis vaccines in the fifth edition of Vaccines, edited by Plotkin, Orenstein, and Offit. 12. Fine and Clarkson (1982) examined the recurrence of whooping cough and its implications for vaccine efficacy assessment in The Lancet. 13. Onorato et al. (1991) explored mucosal immunity induced by enhanced-potency inactivated and oral polio vaccines in The Journal of Infectious Diseases. 14. Plotkin and Vidor (2008) reviewed inactivated polio vaccines in the fifth edition of Vaccines. 15. Sutter, Kew, and Cochi (2008) discussed live polio vaccines in the same edition of Vaccines. 16. Gravenstein et al. (1994) evaluated the efficacy of an influenza hemagglutinin-diphtheria toxoid conjugate vaccine in elderly nursing home residents during an influenza outbreak, published in Journal of the American Geriatrics Society. 17. McElhaney et al. (2006) demonstrated that T-cell responses are better correlates of vaccine protection in the elderly, as reported in The Journal of Immunology. 18. Jodar et al. (2003) established serological criteria for evaluating and licensing new pneumococcal conjugate vaccine formulations for infants, published in Vaccine. 19. Fine (1995) discussed variations in protection by BCG and its implications for heterologous immunity in The Lancet. 20. Itoh et al. (2002) conducted a comparative analysis of antibody titers against measles virus in vaccinated and naturally infected Japanese individuals across different age groups, published in Journal of Clinical Microbiology. 21. Jelonek et al. (1993) compared naturally acquired and vaccine-induced antibodies to Haemophilus influenzae type b capsular polysaccharide in Infection and Immunity. 22. Schlesinger and Granoff (1992) studied the avidity and bactericidal activity of antibodies elicited by different Haemophilus influenzae type b conjugate vaccines, published in JAMA. 23. Edwards et al. (1995) compared 13 acellular pertussis vaccines, focusing on serologic responses, as reported in Pediatrics. 24. Denoel et al. (2007) evaluated the quality of Haemophilus influenzae type b antibody responses induced by diphtheria-tetanus-acellular pertussis/Hib combination vaccines in Clinical Vaccine Immunology. 25. The WHO (2005) provided recommendations for the production and control of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines in its Technical Report Series No. 927. 26. Schuerman et al. (2007) analyzed ELISA IgG concentrations and opsonophagocytic activity following pneumococcal protein D conjugate vaccination and their relationship to efficacy against acute otitis media, published in Vaccine. 27. Olin et al. (2001) discussed the interpretation of pertussis immunogenicity data in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 28. Hadler et al. (1986) examined the long-term immunogenicity and efficacy of the hepatitis B vaccine in homosexual men, as reported in The New England Journal of Medicine. 29. Szmuness et al. (1980) demonstrated the efficacy of the hepatitis B vaccine in a controlled clinical trial involving a high-risk population in the United States, published in The New England Journal of Medicine. 30. Amanna, Carlson, and Slifka (2007) studied the duration of humoral immunity to common viral and vaccine antigens in The New England Journal of Medicine. 31. Rothman, Greenland, and Lash (2008) authored Modern Epidemiology, a comprehensive resource on epidemiological methods. 32. Feavers et al. (2009) discussed challenges in evaluating and licensing new pneumococcal vaccines during a meeting in Ottawa, Canada, published in Vaccine. 33. Smith, Rodrigues, and Fine (1984) assessed the protective efficacy of vaccines against common diseases using case-control and cohort studies in International Journal of Epidemiology. 34. Halloran, Haber, and Longini (1992) explored the interpretation and estimation of vaccine efficacy under heterogeneity in American Journal of Epidemiology. 35. Haber, Watlet, and Halloran (1995) examined individual and population effectiveness of vaccination in International Journal of Epidemiology. 36. White et al. 37. Plotkin (2008) reviewed correlates of vaccine-induced immunity in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 38. Plotkin (2010) discussed correlates of protection induced by vaccination in Clinical Vaccine Immunology. 39. The FDA (1992) proposed regulations for accelerated approval of new drugs, antibiotics, and biological products in the Federal Register. 40. Tiernan provided a regulatory perspective on developing preventive vaccines for global infectious diseases. 41. The ICH (1997) issued a harmonized tripartite guideline on general considerations for clinical trials (E8). 42. The ICH (1998) released a guideline on statistical principles for clinical trials (E9). 43. The European Medicines Agency (1999) provided guidance on the clinical evaluation of new vaccines. 44. The WHO (2004) published guidelines on the clinical evaluation of vaccines, outlining regulatory expectations in its Technical Report Series No. 924.
